findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are hardcoded in plaintext within the instance user_data script, which is visible via the EC2 metadata service and Terraform state, risking credential leakage.
The EBS volume does not have encryption enabled (encrypted attribute is commented out), leaving data at rest unprotected.
The EBS snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and has no encryption configured, exposing data at rest.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the instance to brute-force and unauthorized access attempts from any source on the internet.

The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no additional restrictions, which combined with unrestricted egress broadens the attack surface unnecessarily for a security-sensitive host.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block or bucket policy restricting access, risking exposure of sensitive network log data.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IPs, increasing exposure to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, causing instances launched in this subnet to automatically receive public IPs, increasing exposure to the internet.
